RESULT
Blue vitriol crystals were prepared from the mixture* of copper sulphate and common salt by different chemical actions followed by filtration and crystallization.
PRECAUTIONS
All the copper sulphate should be converted into cupric oxide.
There should not be any loss of black oxide of copper.
The solution of copper sulphate should not be overheated.
The crystals of blue vitriol should not be dried over the Bunsen burner. (Answer why?)
Care should be taken while collecting the crystals on a filter paper so that the shape of the crystals does not get disturbed.
Addition of too much H2S04 should be avoided otherwise the shape of the crystals will be disturbed.
Separation of Mixtures Note:
1. Big crystals can be obtained when the solution is allowed to stand for a
long time. Rapid cooling does not give good crystals. On the other hand, a long cooling ntay contaminate the crystals due to cooling of the mother liquor.
2. Repeated crystallization can be done to get the pure crystals.
SUGGESTED WORKS
1. To prepare barium chloride crystals from the mixture of barium
chloride and common salt.
2. To prepare copper sulphate crystals from the mixture of black oxide
of copper and charcoal. (Hints: Dissolve the mixture in water, leave for some time, charcoal floats on the surface, remove it, dissolve cupric oxide in dil. H2S04 and carry out crystallisation).

PROCEDURE

Glass rod Liquid Fitter paper Filtrate Figure 2.17: Filtration Take the given mixture of zinc carbonate and magnesium carbonate l. in a beaker. Add dilute hydrochloric acid just to dissolve the mixture till effervescences cease.
Add sodium hydroxide solution so as to obtain a white precipitate.
Zinc •hydroxide gets converted into soluble sodium zincate but not magnesium hydroxide.
Heat the solution for some time. Allow it to stand over the asbestos sheet for some time to settle down the precipitate.

Practical Chemistry To ensure the complete precipitation, add a drop of dilute sodium hydroxide to the supernatant liquid. If a fresh white e precipitate appears, this indicates that all the zinc hydroxide is not converted into soluble zincate.
Add few more drops of dilute sodium hydroxide. Check Uthe completeness of precipitation as before.
When no more fresh precipitate appears, filter the solution.

Neutralize the solution by adding dilute sulphuric acid. The solution can be inboduced on blue and red litmus papers to know whether the soluüon is neutral or not. If excess of acid is added, then neuåalize the solution by adding few drops of dilute sodium hydroxide.
Filter the solution if it looks dirty. Transfer the solution in a porcelain basin. Place it over the sand bath and heat upto the crystallization point.

To ascertain the crystallization point, introduce with the help of a glass rod, few drops of the evaporated solution on the outer wall of the test tube filled with cold water. Colourless crystals are seen when the solution attains the crystallization point.
